title.narrative: The capacity of ILO constituents and key actors to address the worst forms of child labour is enhanced and the knowledge base on child labour is improved

description.narrative:
Child labour deprives children of their basic human rights including their right to education and to develop their full potential. It often involves dangerous and exploitative working conditions that can have serious negative impacts on children's physical and mental health. More so, it poses a salient human rights risk for many businesses and continues to be a significant concern for governments and consumers globally. There is a growing recognition that focusing solely on workplace monitoring and remediation, and on immediate suppliers, without addressing the root causes of the problem at the lower tiers of the supply chain, will not make a sustainable impact on the long-term elimination of child labour and may simply displace children from one supply chain to another. The ILO’s experience fighting child labour has shown that eliminating child labour at the national level requires adequately financed and effectively implemented public policies that are clearly designed to address its root causes.
Therefore, the ILO’s intervention is designed to accelerate progress on the eradication of forced labour and the elimination of child labour by optimizing the effectiveness of development cooperation interventions and resources. It also promotes decent work in supply chains globally and in Africa for several years.
